title: Revealing the structure of language model capabilities
claim: LLM capabilities on HELM are not monolithic: three factors (comprehension, language modeling, reasoning) explain performance better than a single g; factors relate differently to model size.
models: 29 HELM LLMs (2022-era, e.g., GPT-3 variants, OPT, BLOOM, GLM, etc.)
supporting_quotes: We found evidence that LLM capabilities are not monolithic.
a 3-factor solution is most appropriate
model size was more strongly correlated with comprehension than with either language modeling or reasoning
social_or_spatial_tasks_included: No ToM or spatial task. Closest: BBQ (bias, loads on reasoning F3), HellaSwag (commonsense, loads on comprehension F1).
relevance: Shows co-movement across tasks is substantial and partly driven by size, but structured (>1 factor). Neither spatial nor social measured, so cannot answer the specific link.
verification: Numbers read from arXiv HTML (Table 2, Table 3) via fetch; full task list in Fig. 1 not inspected.

title: Observational Scaling Laws and the Predictability of Language Model Performance
claim: Benchmark performance of ~100 public LLMs lies in a low-dimensional capability space; PC1 is a general capability factor that is linear in log-compute within families, and predicts emergent and agentic abilities.

key_numbers.PC1_vs_log_FLOPs_within_family: R^2 > 0.9 (as summarized by fetch; not verified verbatim)
key_numbers.PCs: PC1 general, PC2 reasoning (math/code), PC3 programming

models: ~77-100 public base LLMs (Llama, Qwen, Mistral, etc.) on MMLU, ARC-C, HellaSwag, Winogrande, TruthfulQA, GSM8K, XWinograd, HumanEval
supporting_quotes: model performance is a function of a low-dimensional capability space, and model families only vary in their efficiency
the first PC alone explains nearly 80% of the variation in LM capabilities
social_or_spatial_tasks_included: No ToM/social or spatial benchmark among the base benchmarks.
relevance: Strongest evidence that any two benchmark scores across models will co-move largely through a single general (compute-driven) factor; this is the null hypothesis a spatial-social correlation must beat.
verification: Abstract quote verbatim; 80%/97% quoted from HTML via fetch; R^2>0.9 figure is the fetch tool's paraphrase.

title: Evidence of interrelated cognitive-like capabilities in large language models: Indications of artificial general intelligence or achievement?
claim: Open LLM Leaderboard scores show a positive manifold and a general factor; parameter count correlates moderately with g with diminishing returns.

published_version.note: g plus a Gkn/Grw group factor; size correlates with both

models: Open LLM Leaderboard open-weight models (ARC, HellaSwag, TruthfulQA, MMLU subtests)
supporting_quotes: accounts for 85% of the variance in model performance (v1)
moderate correlation of .48 between model size and g (v1)
found strong empirical evidence for a positive manifold and a general factor of ability (published abstract)
the number of LLM parameters correlated positively with both general factor of ability and Gkn/Grw factor scores
relevance: Direct support for 'general factor' explanation of co-movement; size explains only part (r~.48) of g.
verification: 85% and r=.48 are from v1 HTML (2310.11616v1); published 591-model version numbers for variance not verified.

title: A Neuropsychologically Grounded Evaluation of LLM Cognitive Abilities (NeuroCognition)
topic: general factor (g) in LLMs, incl. spatial working memory
claim: Factor analysis of 156 LLMs on 10 Artificial Analysis benchmarks yields one dominant factor; their NeuroCognition battery (Raven's, Spatial Working Memory, WCST) average correlates highly with general benchmark average.
models: 156 LLMs (Artificial Analysis leaderboard) for EFA; 10 models for NeuroCognition
supporting_quotes: This factor (PA1) accounted for 75% of the total variance
all benchmarks had high loadings (λ>0.76)
high correlation between the average NeuroCognition score and the 11-benchmark average (r=.86,p=.001,N=10)
social_or_spatial_tasks_included: Spatial working memory (in NeuroCognition); no social/ToM.
relevance: Recent frontier-model evidence of a strong g (75%); a spatial-ish cognitive test tracks general benchmarks at the aggregate level.
verification: Benchmark list inferred by fetch tool from citations; numbers quoted from HTML.

title: Quantifying construct validity in large language model evaluations
claim: Latent factors extracted from benchmark matrices often just proxy model size; proposes a structured capabilities model that conditions on scale.
supporting_quotes: Latent factor models ignore scaling laws, and as a result, the capabilities they extract often proxy model size.
relevance: Supports controlling for size/general factor before claiming a specific spatial-social link.

title: From Benchmarks to Skills: Low-Rank Factors for LLM Evaluation
claim: 60 models x 44 tasks reduce to 8 latent skill dimensions; a 'Social/Ethical Judgment' factor exists but loads on CivilComments/MMLU, not ToM.
supporting_quotes: uncovered 8 latent dimensions
relevance: Shows multi-factor structure once many tasks are used; no evidence on spatial-social.
verification: Authors/numbers from partial HTML fetch; first-factor variance not found.

title: Redundancy Principles for MLLMs Benchmarks
claim: Across >100 MLLMs (VLMEvalKit), MMBench capability dimensions are highly rank-correlated, especially among weaker models; Spatial Relationship is highly redundant with many dimensions, and Social Relation is strongly redundant with Image Emotion. Redundancy drops for stronger models.

key_numbers.pairwise_spatial_vs_social: only in heatmaps (Fig. 3/4), not in text

models: >100 MLLMs from VLMEvalKit/OpenCompass; split Top-50/Bottom-50 by MMBench overall
supporting_quotes: For example, the tasks Image Emotion and Social Relation display strong redundancy.
Conversely, high levels of redundancy are observed for Nature Relation and Spatial Relationship.
This phenomenon can primarily be attributed to the fact that Bottom-50 MLLMs generally underperform across all capabilities.
the dimensions appear to be more redundant for Bottom-50 MLLMs than for Top-50 MLLMs
social_or_spatial_tasks_included: Yes: MMBench 'Spatial Relationship' and 'Social Relation' (both image-level). Pairwise value not stated in text.
relevance: Only paper found whose correlation matrix contains both a spatial and a social dimension; its explanation is a general factor (weak models bad at everything), and the co-movement weakens among strong models.
verification: Quotes verbatim from HTML; I could not read the heatmap value for Spatial Relationship x Social Relation.

title: Cambrian-1: A Fully Open, Vision-Centric Exploration of Multimodal LLMs
claim: PCA over 23 MLLMs clusters benchmarks into General, Knowledge, Chart/OCR, Vision-Centric; many benchmarks mostly measure the LLM; vision-centric (incl. spatial: CV-Bench depth/relation/distance) form a separate cluster.

key_numbers.vision_off_gap: SQA-I, MMMU, MathVista, AI2D <5% gap vision on vs off

supporting_quotes: Most benchmarks do not properly measure vision-centric capabilities, and the ones that do have very few samples.
relevance: Spatial/vision-centric ability is partly separable from the LLM-driven 'general/knowledge' cluster, and scaling LLM size gives non-monotonic spatial gains.
verification: Numbers from Table 9 via fetch; non-monotonic reading is mine.

title: Thinking in Space: How Multimodal Large Language Models See, Remember, and Recall Spaces (VSI-Bench)
claim: Spatial reasoning is the main bottleneck; larger variants within a family score higher, but linguistic prompting (CoT, ToT) hurts spatial performance while helping general video QA.
models: 15 MLLMs incl. GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5, LLaVA-OV, LLaVA-Video, InternVL2
supporting_quotes: around 71% of errors are attributed to spatial reasoning
harmful for spatial reasoning (on linguistic prompting)
relevance: Spatial scales with size moderately but not uniformly; general/linguistic reasoning tools don't transfer to spatial, arguing against a single shared reasoning factor for spatial.

title: Has GPT-5 Achieved Spatial Intelligence? An Empirical Study (EASI)
claim: Across 8 spatial benchmarks, GPT-5 is strongest yet far below humans; spatial tasks are much harder than non-spatial subtasks; within-family size helps.
models: GPT-5 family, Gemini, Claude, InternVL3, Qwen2.5-VL, etc.
supporting_quotes: Spatial intelligence (SI) tasks pose significantly greater challenges than non-SI tasks.
relevance: Spatial does improve with scale/generation, but the paper reports no correlation with general benchmarks and treats SI as a distinct skill.
verification: Size numbers are fetch-tool reading of Table 6 (authors make no explicit scaling claim).

title: SITE: towards Spatial Intelligence Thorough Evaluation
claim: SITE scores correlate with robotic manipulation (LIBERO-Spatial), but general benchmarks like MathVista correlate as well or better (n=4 models).
supporting_quotes: have a positive Pearson Correlation Coefficient of 0.902
relevance: Illustrates that a general multimodal benchmark (MathVista) predicts downstream spatial behavior as well as a spatial benchmark: consistent with a general factor; n=4 so fragile.

title: SpatialScore: Towards Unified Evaluation for Multimodal Spatial Understanding
claim: Larger models generally better on spatial; authors attribute to stronger intrinsic reasoning, but gains saturate (Qwen2.5-VL 32B->72B +1.2).
supporting_quotes: Larger models generally exhibit stronger performance, as observed in both the InternVL
This trend suggests that stronger intrinsic reasoning ability can translate into improved spatial intelligence.
relevance: Spatial scales roughly log-linearly with size within families; authors' interpretation invokes general reasoning.

title: OmniSpatial: Towards Comprehensive Spatial Reasoning Benchmark for Vision Language Models
claim: Size mostly helps (InternVL3 2B->78B: 37.98->49.33) but not always (Qwen2.5-VL 3B>7B); allocentric/hypothetical perspective-taking is near-flat across frontier models (~38-48 vs human ~90-94).
models: o3, GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-Pro, InternVL3, Qwen2.5-VL, Gemma-3, LLaVA-OV
supporting_quotes: especially with geometric reasoning and non-egocentric perspective taking
relevance: Perspective-taking (the putative spatial-social bridge) is the least scale-responsive spatial skill.

title: Defining and Evaluating Visual Language Models' Basic Spatial Abilities: A Perspective from Psychometrics
claim: On psychometric basic spatial abilities, smaller models often beat larger ones.
supporting_quotes: Smaller models such as Qwen2-VL-7B surpass larger counterparts, with Qwen leading (30.82) and InternVL2 lagging (19.6).
relevance: Counter-evidence to smooth spatial scaling.

title: LRR-Bench: Left, Right or Rotate? Vision-Language models Still Struggle With Spatial Understanding Tasks
claim: Increasing model size, 3D-data fine-tuning and RL do not consistently improve spatial performance; Qwen2.5-VL 72B gains strongly on composite position tasks but 7B beats 72B on basic Position.
supporting_quotes: increasing model size, fine-tuning on specific 3D datasets and incorporating reinforcement learning (do not consistently enhance performance)
relevance: Spatial scaling is task-dependent and non-monotonic.
verification: Conclusion clause verbatim; parenthetical is paraphrase.

title: Why Do MLLMs Struggle with Spatial Understanding? A Systematic Analysis from Data to Architecture
claim: Spatial performance saturates quickly with data and depends on the vision encoder's positional encoding more than the LLM.
supporting_quotes: the performance of spatial understanding converges quickly as the training data increases
spatial understanding relies more heavily on the positional encoding within the visual encoder ... than within the language model
relevance: If spatial is bottlenecked by the vision encoder while social/ToM is LLM-driven, spatial and social should not share a specific mechanism; co-movement would come via LLM-general factor only.

title: Scaling and Beyond: Advancing Spatial Reasoning in MLLMs Requires New Recipes
claim: Spatial reasoning will not emerge from scaling alone.
supporting_quotes: spatial reasoning capabilities will not naturally emerge from merely scaling existing architectures
relevance: Opinion, no data.

title: Visual Spatial Tuning (VST)
claim: Authors state prior spatial add-ons usually harm general capabilities; their own spatial SFT/RL largely preserves MMBench/OCRBench but MMMU drops notably at 7B.
supporting_quotes: which brings extra overhead and usually harms general capabilities
relevance: Spatial gains can come at the cost of knowledge/reasoning (MMMU -8 to -9 pts at 7B): spatial specialization does not ride a shared general factor upward.
verification: Table 2 numbers via fetch; the MMMU-drop interpretation is mine, not the authors'.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Theory of Mind Tasks
claim: False-belief performance rises across successive GPT generations: older/smaller models solve none, GPT-3 davinci-003 and GPT-3.5 20%, GPT-4 75%.
supporting_quotes: Smaller and older models solved no tasks
may have spontaneously emerged as a byproduct of LLMs' improving language skills
relevance: Most-cited 'ToM scales with capability' result; confounds size, data, RLHF across GPT generations; contested (Ullman 2023, Shapira 2023).

title: Neural Theory-of-Mind? On the Limits of Social Intelligence in Large LMs
claim: GPT-3 well below human on SocialIQa and ToMi; scale alone is argued insufficient.
supporting_quotes: well-below-human accuracies of 55% and 60% on SocialIQa and ToMi, respectively
Challenging the prevalent narrative that only scale is needed
relevance: Classic counterpoint: social reasoning gains with scale are weak.

title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models (Table 3)
claim: Social IQa barely moves with scale compared with HellaSwag/WinoGrande.
supporting_quotes: Most notably, on SIQA, we observe a lot of variance in performance, that may indicate that this benchmark is not reliable. (re: training dynamics)
relevance: Zero-shot social commonsense was nearly flat (+3.4 pts over ~9x params) in base models; social reasoning did not scale smoothly in pre-RLHF models.

title: FANToM: A Benchmark for Stress-testing Machine Theory of Mind in Interactions
claim: Near-zero All* scores regardless of size; GPT-4 far below humans; CoT helps little.
supporting_quotes: score significantly lower than humans
does not substantially bridge the gap with human performance (re CoT)
relevance: No size trend on robust (consistency-requiring) ToM.

title: ToMBench: Benchmarking Theory of Mind in Large Language Models
claim: Parameter count does not predict ToM: Mistral-7B > Llama2-13B; Mixtral-8x7B not > Mistral-7B; GPT-4 ~10 pts below humans.
supporting_quotes: contrasts to its task-solving performance and also underscores the unique nature of ToM evaluation (re Mixtral)
relevance: Explicitly notes ToM rank order diverges from general task-solving rank order for Mixtral: evidence against a pure g account.

title: OpenToM: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Theory-of-Mind Reasoning Capabilities of LLMs
topic: ToM scaling; physical (location) vs psychological states
claim: Within Llama-2 7B->70B some ToM question types improve, others decline (2nd-order coarse location 0.462->0.280); all models poor on psychological attitudes.
supporting_quotes: all LLMs performed poorly on Att questions
relevance: ToM scaling is non-monotonic and question-type dependent.

title: Hi-ToM: A Benchmark for Evaluating Higher-Order Theory of Mind Reasoning in LLMs
claim: Performance declines with higher-order ToM.
supporting_quotes: indicates a decline in performance on higher-order ToM tasks, demonstrating the limitations of current LLMs
relevance: Recursion depth, not scale.

title: LLMs achieve adult human performance on higher-order theory of mind tasks (MoToMQA)
claim: GPT-4 and Flan-PaLM reach (near) adult-level; interplay of size and fine-tuning.
supporting_quotes: there is an interplay between model size and finetuning for the realisation of ToM abilities
GPT-4 and Flan-PaLM reach adult-level and near adult-level performance on ToM tasks overall
relevance: ToM gains depend on size x post-training, not size alone.

title: Traces of Social Competence in Large Language Models
authors: Kouwenhoven, van der Meer, van Duijn
claim: Across 17 open-weight models, size benefits false-belief performance, but not strictly.
supporting_quotes: scaling model size benefits performance, but not strictly
relevance: Recent controlled evidence of positive but non-monotonic ToM scaling.
verification: Abstract only; the true-belief harm claim from a search snippet was NOT verified in the abstract.

title: Developmental Trajectories of Situation Modeling and Mentalizing in Transformer Language Models
topic: ToM scaling over size and training (Pythia/OLMo-2)
claim: Above-chance false-belief performance requires both size and training volume, emerges late, and is most improved by post-training.
supporting_quotes: above-chance FBT performance depends both on model size and sufficient training volume
relevance: Best controlled checkpoint-level evidence; ToM not smooth, late-emerging.

title: MindGames: Targeting Theory of Mind in LLMs with Dynamic Epistemic Modal Logic
claim: Pythia 70M-6.9B and GPT-3 scaling do not consistently beat chance on epistemic logic; GPT-4 better.
relevance: Negative scaling evidence for formal ToM.
verification: Claim from search-result summary only; NOT verified against paper text.

title: Do Theory of Mind Benchmarks Need Explicit Human-like Reasoning in Language Models?
claim: RL on ToM yields good belief-tracking reasoning at 7B but 'reasoning collapse' at <=3B; SFT competitive; benchmarks may be shortcut-solvable.
supporting_quotes: fosters high-quality, interpretable, and transferable belief-tracking reasoning
relevance: ToM gains are scale-dependent and benchmark-shortcut prone.

title: EgoNormia: Benchmarking Physical Social Norm Understanding
topic: social norms in video; failure modes
claim: VLM failures on egocentric norm questions are mostly normative reasoning, not perception; the authors ASSUME (do not test) that normative reasoning scales with general reasoning.
supporting_quotes: gaps in normative reasoning (>70% of errors), rather than perception (<25% of errors)
We assume that normative reasoning scales strongly with general reasoning capability
relevance: Perception (incl. spatial/visual grounding) is not the main bottleneck for social-norm failures, which argues against spatial ability being the limiting factor for social performance.

title: Egocentric Bias in Vision-Language Models (FlipSet)
claim: 103 VLMs mostly below chance on Level-2 visual perspective taking; they pass ToM and mental-rotation controls separately but fail when both must be integrated.
supporting_quotes: the vast majority perform below chance
fail catastrophically when integration is required
relevance: Most direct evidence that spatial and social competences are separable in VLMs: having both does not yield their composition.

title: CogToM: A Comprehensive Theory of Mind Benchmark inspired by Human Cognition for LLMs
claim: Within family/release, larger models are more accurate; the Percept (visual perspective) category is the bottleneck (~20% median).
supporting_quotes: within the same model family and release window, larger parameter counts directly correlate with higher accuracy
median accuracy of only approximately 20%
relevance: ToM scales within family; spatial-perspective ToM lags far behind other ToM.
verification: HTML via fetch; no per-pair numbers.

title: Triangulating LLM Progress through Benchmarks, Games, and Cognitive Tests
topic: correlation of social/ToM tests with general benchmarks
claim: Across 9 open-weight models, cognitive tests correlate with benchmarks/games; ToM (SimpleToM) correlates better with interactive games than static benchmarks (MMLU/BBH).

key_numbers.correlation: Kendall tau-b; values only in Fig. 3

models: Phi-4-mini, OLMo-2 7B/13B, Falcon3-10B, Qwen2.5 7B/32B/72B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.3-70B
supporting_quotes: Among the social skills, pragmatics appears to be relevant for both static and interactive tests, while ToM correlates better with the latter.
social_or_spatial_tasks_included: ToM, SocialIQa, EQ-Bench, pragmatics; no spatial.
relevance: ToM is not simply a static-benchmark (g) proxy; note Llama-3.1-8B ~ Qwen-72B on SimpleToM (ceiling).
verification: Quote verbatim; tau values not readable.

title: MMToM-QA: Multimodal Theory of Mind Question Answering
claim: LLMs and LMMs lack robust ToM on video+text household scenarios.
supporting_quotes: large language models and large multimodal models still lack robust ToM capacity
relevance: Combines spatial navigation and belief inference but reports no correlation/scaling analysis.

title: Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?
claim: Apparent emergence is an artifact of nonlinear metrics; continuous metrics show smooth change.
supporting_quotes: emergent abilities appear due to the researcher's choice of metric
relevance: Relevant to interpreting Kosinski-style 'ToM emerges' step curves.
verification: Abstract via fetch (quote is fetch-tool paraphrase-level; check before citing verbatim).

title: Testing theory of mind in large language models and humans
claim: GPT-4 at/above human on most ToM tests but fails faux pas (hyperconservatism); LLaMA2-70B below humans except an illusory faux-pas edge.
relevance: ToM profile differs across tests, not a single scale-driven trait.
verification: From search summaries only; NOT read in full.

title: Spatial ability and theory of mind: A mediating role of visual perspective taking (Child Development 92(4):1590-1604)
claim: In 3.5-4-year-olds, spatial ability relates to ToM via visual perspective taking (correlational n=70; block-building training n=46 improved VPT and ToM).
supporting_quotes: Study 1 demonstrated such mediation correlationally in seventy 3.5-to 4-year olds.
relevance: Human motivation for a spatial->social link, specifically via perspective taking; no LLM analogue found.
verification: Abstract page only; no effect sizes.
